edges.rationale: SFT requires a pre-trained base model as its starting point; it cannot be performed without first completing pre-training.
Preference finetuning typically starts from an SFT model and uses human feedback to further align its outputs; SFT provides the conversational baseline that preference optimization refines.
Architectural and hyperparameter choices must be made before pre-training begins, as they directly determine how the model is trained and its resulting capabilities.
Design decisions such as model architecture and training setup influence how SFT is conducted and what configurations are used during instruction tuning.
Training design choices affect the base model and SFT checkpoint that preference finetuning builds upon, and can influence alignment hyperparameters.
